patient_information: A 31-year-old woman from northern Tanzania, married with 3 children (last born 12 months old), non-smoker, non-alcoholic, with negative HIV status during her last pregnancy.
chief_complaint: Acute loss of power and feeling in her legs.
history_of_present_illness: She developed acute back pain radiating band-like to her umbilicus, which was severe, continuous, burning, and unrelieved by analgesics or position; within 12 hours, the pain lessened, but she developed numbness in her feet and legs ascending to her waist, loss of power in her legs, and loss of bladder control.
exposure_and_epidemiology: She had a febrile illness 3 weeks prior, treated as malaria.
physical_exam: Well nourished, general examination unremarkable with no spinal tenderness, deformity, or gibbus. Neurological examination showed full orientation, normal higher mental functions, normal cranial nerves including fundoscopy and upper limbs. Lower limbs revealed flaccid paraparesis with a sensory level at T10, plantar-flexed feet, reduced tone bilaterally, reduced power (MRC grade 1/5) in all muscle groups, absent reflexes bilaterally, extensor plantar reflexes, reduced light touch sensation to the umbilicus, impaired joint position sense in feet and ankles, and absent vibration sense to the anterior iliac crest bilaterally.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count, renal and liver function tests were normal. ESR was 19 mm/h, random blood glucose 5.6 mmol/l. HIV-Serology and p24 Antigen, VDRL, Schistosomiasis-serology, urine for ova of S. haematobium, and stool for ova of S. mansoni were all negative. CSF opening pressure was normal, appearance clear. CSF showed a white cell count of 11 cells/µl (90% lymphocytes), protein 1.11 g/L, glucose 3.9 mmol/l, and was negative for Gram stain, Ziehl-Neelsen stain, Xpert MTB/RIF, and VDRL. X-rays of chest and thoracolumbar spine were normal.
differential_diagnosis: Acute spinal cord inflammation (acute transverse myelitis), vascular spinal cord ischaemia ("spinal stroke"), and lesions of peripheral nerves (polyneuropathies or polyradiculoneuropathies) or acute lesions of the spinal cord (myelopathies) were considered.
management_and_clinical_course: Treatment included corticosteroids and acyclovir, along with general measures like strict 2-hourly turning, frequent passive movements, urinary catheterization for non-functioning bladder, and adequate analgesia. The patient partially improved with power in her legs slightly improved to MRC 2-3/5 and was discharged after 3 weeks with a urinary catheter in situ, with follow-up in the outpatient department.
